bib.title: Foundations of Convex Analysis (Chapter 26, Bandit Algorithms)
bib.venue: Book chapter, Bandit Algorithms, Cambridge University Press

question: Which facts from convex analysis (convexity, Jensen, Bregman divergence, Legendre functions, projections) are needed for the mirror-descent and FTRL analyses in later chapters?
contributions: Definitions and statements without proofs; proofs are left as exercises or referred to Rockafellar [2015].

results.claim: A function is convex iff its epigraph is convex; local minima of convex functions are global.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26
results.quote:
The field of optimisation is obsessed with convex functions
because all local minimums are global

results.claim: Jensen: E[f(X)] >= f(E[X]) for measurable convex f; direction reverses for concave.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26

results.claim: Bregman divergence is non-negative, zero at x=y, convex in x for differentiable y, but not symmetric and no triangle inequality.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26
results.quote:
In
general, however, it is not symmetric and does not satisfy the triangle inequality.

results.claim: With f=1/2||x||^2 the Bregman divergence is half squared Euclidean distance.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26

results.claim: With the unnormalised negentropy, the Bregman divergence on the simplex is relative entropy (KL).
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26
results.quote:
Notice that if x, y ∈Pd−1 are in the unit simplex, then Df(x, y) is the relative
entropy between probability vectors x and y.

results.claim: For Legendre f, grad f is a bijection with inverse grad f*, and Df(x,y)=Df*(grad f(y), grad f(x)).
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26
results.quote: Df(x, y) = Df ∗(∇f(y), ∇f(x)) for all x, y ∈int(dom(f))

results.claim: A Legendre minimiser over its domain lies in the interior (gradient blows up at boundary).
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26

results.claim: Exact second-order form: Df(x,y)=1/2 (x-y)^T Hessian(z) (x-y) for some z on the segment.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26

results.claim: Key inequality for regret bounds: <x-y,u> - Df(x,y)/eta <= (eta/2)||u||^2 in the inverse-Hessian norm at some z between x and y.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26

results.claim: For Legendre f, minimising f over closed convex A equals Bregman-projecting the unconstrained minimiser onto A.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26

results.claim: Exercise 26.11(b): Bregman projection of y onto simplex under negentropy is y/||y||_1 (normalisation); 26.12 gives clipped-simplex solution.
results.setup: Convex f on R^d, Lattimore & Szepesvari ch. 26

limits: No proofs: Theorems 26.3, 26.6, 26.12, 26.15 and Prop 26.7, 26.14 are left to exercises or Rockafellar [2015].
No bandit algorithm or regret bound appears; the chapter is purely preparatory.
Topology (interior, boundary, closed) is given only for R^d.

terms.definition: A set A in R^d is convex if alpha x+(1-alpha)y is in A for all x,y in A and alpha in (0,1).
The smallest convex set containing the points; co(x1..xn) = sum p_i x_i with p in the simplex.
Ef = {(x,y): y >= f(x)}; f is convex iff Ef is convex.
Range excludes -infinity and domain is nonempty.
f*(u)=sup_x <x,u> - f(x); f=f** when f is proper convex with closed epigraph.
Df(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-grad_{x-y} f(y), the gap between f(x) and its linearisation at y.
f(x)=sum_i (x_i log x_i - x_i) on [0,inf)^d; gives relative entropy on the simplex.
Convex f with non-empty interior of domain, differentiable and strictly convex there, and gradient norm to infinity approaching the boundary.
x* in argmin_A f iff <x-x*, grad f(x*)> >= 0 for all x in A.
